findings.description: The RDS instance explicitly sets storage_encrypted = false, leaving database storage and associated snapshots unencrypted at rest. Anyone obtaining access to the underlying storage or a snapshot is not protected by an encryption key.

The RDS instance sets publicly_accessible = true, which assigns a public network endpoint to the database. Although the shown security-group ingress is VPC-scoped, exposing the database publicly unnecessarily expands its network attack surface and makes later security-group errors externally exploitable.

This rule permits all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0 from the database security group. A compromised database instance could communicate with arbitrary external hosts for data exfiltration or command-and-control.

The EC2 role grants all S3, EC2, and RDS actions against every resource. Compromise of the application instance or its role credentials would grant broad control over these services, including access to data and the ability to alter infrastructure.

The database password is interpolated into EC2 user_data and written into a PHP configuration file. User data is readable through instance metadata and EC2 describe APIs to principals with access, exposing the database credential beyond a dedicated secrets store.
No metadata_options configuration requires IMDSv2, so the instance may permit IMDSv1. An SSRF flaw in the web application could then retrieve instance-role credentials from the metadata service.

The instance does not configure an encrypted root_block_device. Unless an account-level EBS encryption-by-default setting exists outside this configuration, the application filesystem—including the database credential file written by user data—can be stored unencrypted at rest.
